subject.title: fix(android): keep composer media with its chat

question: Should Android upgrades intentionally park legacy ownerless outbox rows as non-retryable recovery entries requiring manual re-entry or deletion?
rationale: The safe original owner cannot be reconstructed, but changing previously queued durable work into manual recovery is a user-visible upgrade contract that model judgment cannot authorize despite the strong implementation.

options.title: Approve after upgrade proof
options.body: Accept fail-closed recovery after exact-head tests demonstrate migration from the shipped database, visible recovery rows, deletion, and no cross-owner replay.

options.title: Add explicit reassignment flow
options.body: Delay merge and design a user-confirmed owner-selection flow for legacy rows, accepting greater complexity to preserve more queued content.

options.title: Narrow the landing
options.body: Split the original composer-media isolation fix from the wider cache, outbox, and gateway ownership migration if the upgrade contract is too broad for this release.

recommendation.title: Approve after upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Accept fail-closed recovery after exact-head tests demonstrate migration from the shipped database, visible recovery rows, deletion, and no cross-owner replay.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the branch's expanded ownership and migration design and is best positioned to approve its intentional upgrade behavior.
